calibration.note: The `formula` block is modelled, not measured: EXPLORATION_CALLS and CALLS_PER_STORY come from the engine's loop ceilings (semantic_tester.py max_iter, orchestrator.py max_steps), not from token logs. It meters BYOK plans, where a credit represents CAPACITY rather than cost, so an approximation is acceptable. Managed plans do not use it — they bill from `modelRates` against tokens the engine actually reported.

meters.note: Which meter each plan family bills on. BYOK customers pay their model provider directly, so charging them per token would bill twice for the same call; their credits meter our server capacity via `formula`. On Managed plans we pay the provider, so credits pass that cost through via `modelRates`.

apiTestFormula._comment: The capacity meter for API SECURITY SCANS (api_test_run), the analogue of `formula` for web testing. Same rule applies: BYOK only. Managed API runs bill from modelRates like every other Managed run.
apiTestFormula._calibration: MEASURED, unlike `formula`. Wall-clock duration of real runs against mnr-clipcut.com on 2026-08-12: 27 endpoints/83 tests took 112-159s over 8 runs (mean 145s), and 50 endpoints/222 tests took 447s. Duration is linear in test count at ~1.9s/test (83*1.9=158 vs 145 actual; 222*1.9=422 vs 447 actual) and endpoint count adds nothing separable, being collinear with it. Rounded to 2 for headroom. SECONDS_PER_CREDIT is derived from internal.creditsPerServerMonth: a 30-day server-month is 2592000s over 11000 credits = 236s per credit. Re-measure if the executor's request_delay (0.5s) changes, since that dominates Phase 3.

modelRates._note: USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Anthropic rates are from the published price list. OpenAI rates are UNVERIFIED — confirm against openai.com/api/pricing before enabling Managed billing, because gpt-4.1-mini is the default engine for Managed Starter and Growth.

_cacheMultipliers.note: Cache reads bill at ~0.1x the input rate; 5-minute-TTL cache writes at 1.25x. The engine does not use prompt caching yet, so these are zero in practice — see the caching lever in the pricing doc.

fx.disclaimer: Indicative INR conversion. USD is the contractual currency.
